source: Nanda et al. (2026) Wink: Recovering from Misbehaviors in Coding Agents (recovery rates)
finding: Gap 8. Mid-run course-correction guidance was followed by recovery in most flagged trajectories, but recovery was judged by an LLM judge looking at 15 steps after the nudge. It is not task success.
numbers: 10,554 trajectories from the A/B treatment arm where an intervention fired. Single-intervention: 5,194 trajectories, 90.93% recovered (reasoning problems 94.29%, spec drift 91.63%, tool call failure 87.83%). Multiple interventions: 5,360 trajectories, 79.07% recovered (reasoning 73.78%, tool 78.52%, spec drift 87.92%). Judge precision on hand-checked tens of cases: 85.71%.
limits: Judge labels recovered if the detected misbehaviour does not recur and there is forward progress. No control arm without guidance in this table, so recovery is not an effect size. Deployed only at Meta.
agent_relevance: Mid-run injection reduces visible misbehaviour; the paper never shows it raises final task accuracy. Test accuracy on held-out items, not just fewer loops.

source: Nanda et al. (2026) Wink: Recovering from Misbehaviors in Coding Agents (live A/B)
finding: Gap 8. In a live 15-day A/B test the guidance system gave small relative reductions in cost and failure metrics, not large ones.
numbers: Tool call failure rate 5.07% vs 5.29% control (-4.2%, significant). Tokens per session -5.3%. Engineer interventions per session -4.2%. Execution time -4.3% (p=0.073, not significant). Shadow mode: misbehaviour rate 15.14% with course-correction vs 18.61% detection only (3,864 and 4,168 invocations; z-test p=0.00003). Prevalence 12,499 of 42,807 sampled trajectories (29.2%).
limits: Metrics are process metrics. No task-success or correctness rate reported. Single company, no external replication.
agent_relevance: Effect of guidance is real but small (about 4-5%). It matches the DellaVigna one-sixth pattern: large in the recovery table, small in the live trial. Gap 8 partly closed: it reduces misbehaviour, accuracy untested.

source: Nanda et al. (2026) Wink: Recovering from Misbehaviors in Coding Agents (why recovery fails)
finding: Hand-coded reasons for failure to recover: the agent ignored the guidance most often.
numbers: Recovered cases: infinite loop recovery 39%, reminder of original task with updated plan 26%, do-not-overdo 17%, right tool arguments 17%. Not recovered: agent ignored guidance 37%, premature termination 22% (other categories not read).
limits: Qualitative coding by four team members on a random subset; subset size not stated in the part I read.
agent_relevance: Guidance can be ignored. A scaffold step should log whether the injected text changed the next action.

source: Sclar, Choi, Tsvetkov, Suhr (2024) Quantifying Language Models Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design (ICLR) (size of spread)
finding: Gap 5 and 7. Meaning-preserving format changes alone swing accuracy hugely. The spread does not go away with larger models, more few-shot examples or instruction tuning.
numbers: Up to 76 accuracy points for LLaMA-2-13B between equivalent formats; about 10 points on average across 50+ tasks and several models. Median spread 7.5 points over tasks. GPT-3.5: up to 56 points, median 6.4, over 320 formats and 53 tasks, under 10 USD per task using FormatSpread.
quote: Sensitivity remains even when increasing model size, the number of few-shot examples, or performing instruction tuning.
limits: Older open models (LLaMA-2, Falcon, GPT-3.5), few-shot classification tasks. Frontier reasoning models not tested.
agent_relevance: A single prompt format is a nudge the model cannot ignore. Any scaffold gain must be reported as a range over paraphrases, not one run.

source: Sclar, Choi, Tsvetkov, Suhr (2024) Quantifying Language Models Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design (ICLR) (cross-model correlation)
finding: Gap 5 and 7. Which format is best barely transfers between models, so a scaffold variant that wins on one model is not predicted to win on another.
numbers: Format performance only weakly correlates between models. Authors recommend reporting the interval of performance across plausible formats (FormatSpread, Bayesian optimisation under a compute budget). Spread estimated within 2 points of the true spread in their tests.
limits: Weak correlation, not zero. Measured on open models of 2023.
agent_relevance: Supports per-model measurement of the scaffold (G7). Do not carry a winning variant across model versions without retesting.

source: Meincke, Mollick, Mollick, Shapiro (2025) Prompting Science Report 2: The Decreasing Value of Chain of Thought in Prompting (Wharton GAIL) (non-reasoning models)
finding: Gap 1. An advice-style prompt addition (think step by step) helps non-reasoning models a little on average, but hurts the strict all-correct metric for several, and costs more time. Different wordings of the advice made negligible difference.
numbers: GPQA Diamond, 198 questions x 25 trials = 4,950 runs per prompt per model. CoT vs direct, average rating: Gemini Flash 2.0 +0.135, Sonnet 3.5 +0.117 (both p<.001), GPT-4o-mini +0.044 (p=.067). 25/25-correct metric: Sonnet 3.5 +0.101, GPT-4o +0.01 (ns), Gemini Flash 2.0 -0.131, Gemini Pro 1.5 -0.172. CoT took 35-600% (5-15 s) longer. Versus default (no suffix): Flash 2.0 +0.062, GPT-4o +0.069, Sonnet 3.5 -0.019 (ns), GPT-4o-mini +0.004 (ns).
limits: One benchmark (GPQA multiple choice), temperature 0, five models of 2024-25. The main comparison is against a control told to answer without thinking. URL is the lab home page; the exact report URL was not recorded, text was read from a PDF fetched this session.
agent_relevance: Most of the advice gain is relative to a weak control. Against the model default it is small or zero. Test our scaffold against the default, not against a strawman.

source: Meincke, Mollick, Mollick, Shapiro (2025) Prompting Science Report 2: The Decreasing Value of Chain of Thought in Prompting (Wharton GAIL) (reasoning models and prompt variants)
finding: Gap 1. For reasoning models explicit CoT gave marginal gains or losses with large time and token costs. Four differently worded advice prompts (step by step, think carefully, decompose, weigh paths) made negligible difference.
numbers: o3-mini and o4-mini small significant gains in average (RD +0.029, p=.024; +0.031, p=.003); Gemini Flash 2.5 -0.033 (p=.005). Variant comparison on GPT-4o at 100 samples per question. Threshold metrics: almost no significant changes.
quote: For models designed with explicit reasoning capabilities, CoT prompting often results in only marginal, if any, gains in answer accuracy.
limits: Industry report, not peer reviewed. Single benchmark.
agent_relevance: Advice-style text added to a strong reasoning model is a weak nudge. Structure that changes what the model must produce (format, forced plan) is the better candidate, but this report did not test it.

source: Halimeh, Kaltenpoth, Bosch, Muller (2026) A Dual-Process Perspective on Nudge Susceptibility in LLM-Based GUI Agents (re-opened, effect sizes)
finding: Gap 4. Re-read in full text: default and social-proof effects confirmed (closes the c06 open item). Reasoning is an API setting here, not a reflection step.
numbers: 21,600 interactions, six models, three providers. Pooled odds ratios vs no nudge: default 8.70 (CI 7.54-9.97), social influence 37.24 (CI 31.04-44.20); with provider and size controls 8.94 and 38.69. No-nudge baseline about 50% in both reasoning settings (47-53% and 46-51%). Reasoning alone, no nudge: beta -0.05 (CI -0.21, 0.12).
limits: Preprint, simulated store, versions fixed by name. Two Claude models hit 100% ceilings so estimates there are partly prior-driven.
agent_relevance: Confirms the strongest AI-nudge effect sizes seen so far, but they come from a lab-style store task with the nudge placed in the interface.

source: Halimeh, Kaltenpoth, Bosch, Muller (2026) A Dual-Process Perspective on Nudge Susceptibility in LLM-Based GUI Agents (reasoning interaction)
finding: Gap 4. High reasoning cut default following but raised social-proof following; it shifted the type of pull rather than removing it.
numbers: Default selected: 92% (CI 91-93) no reasoning vs 86% (CI 84-87) high reasoning; odds ratio 0.51 (CI 0.41-0.62). Social influence: about 96% to 98%; odds ratio 1.71 (CI 1.26-2.20). Gemini 3.5 Flash default following 84% to 48%. GPT-5.4-mini social following 91% to 99%; GPT-5.4 no increase.
quote: deliberation did not eliminate behavioural bias in LLM agents. Instead, it changed the type of influence
limits: The authors state prompt-level deliberation instructions were not tested. Scale pattern was not hypothesised and is exploratory.
agent_relevance: A reflection step could lower default pull and raise authority or social-cue pull. Gap 4 stays open for prompt-level reflection: measure both pulls together.

source: Halimeh, Kaltenpoth, Bosch, Muller (2026) A Dual-Process Perspective on Nudge Susceptibility in LLM-Based GUI Agents (scale and version)
finding: Gap 5 and 7. Susceptibility pattern depends on model size class: small models follow defaults more, flagships follow social cues more. Authors warn version updates may change levels.
numbers: Default odds ratio 15.94 (small variants) vs 4.64 (flagships); social influence 107.57 (flagships) vs 17.59 (small). Absolute levels may differ for later versions even under the same name.
limits: Exploratory, few models per size class.
agent_relevance: A moderator for the heterogeneity question (gap 7): model size class. Re-measure after every model version change.

source: Montero-Porras, Abels, Lenaerts (2026) Prompt framing governs LLM default following in collective-action settings (wording variants, re-opened)
finding: Gap 5. Re-read: a model is a fixator or a rejector of an indefensible default depending on the wording, so the label belongs to the model-wording pair. Four wordings V0-V3 tested.
numbers: CPR indefensible default d=26, V0: gpt 5.1 0.98 and gpt 5.4 mini 0.90 fixate; gpt 5.4, nano, Qwen3.5-9B, Llama 3.3 reject (<0.5), Gemma4-31B 0.62. V1: gpt 5.4 0.27 to 0.88, nano 0.33 to 0.86, Qwen 0.27 to 0.90. V2 (permission wording) drops spike to near 0.00 for several models; gpt 5.1 stays 0.97. V3 (instruction) raises spike everywhere. Net pull mean CPR: agreement 0.25 vs conflict 0.58.
limits: Seven models with logprob access, reasoning off, one-shot, no Claude or Gemini. Single group.
agent_relevance: Paraphrase instability is large and measured. Version note: gpt 5.1 did not respond to permission wording like gpt 5.4. Closes the paraphrase half of gap 5; the version half is shown only by that gpt 5.1 vs 5.4 difference.

source: Montero-Porras, Abels, Lenaerts (2026) Prompt framing governs LLM default following in collective-action settings (limitations)
finding: Gap 5. The authors state what the paper cannot say: no persistence over repeated play, no mechanism, model set is not representative.
numbers: Seven models only (Qwen3 235B dropped; a sensitivity check showed no conclusion change). Single-shot design.
quote: the magnitude of that shift is governed more by the wording of the default line than by which model is tested
limits: Wording larger than model is the authors reading; no variance decomposition seen in my read.
agent_relevance: Treat wording as a first-class factor in any scaffold test.

source: Hewitt, Ashokkumar, Ghezae, Willer (2024/2026) Predicting results of social science experiments using large language models (listed as Nature on project page)
finding: Gap 3. GPT-4 simulated responses predicted survey-experiment treatment effects well, but predictions overestimated effect sizes, and on megastudies the correlation was lower.
numbers: 70 preregistered US survey experiments, 469-476 effects, 105,165 to 119,330 participants (versions differ). r=0.85 overall, r=0.90 for unpublished studies (project page). Megastudy archive: 15 megastudies, 606 effects (older page: 346 across nine); correlation lower, comparable to pooled expert forecasters.
quote: Predictions systematically overestimated effect sizes despite high correlations.
limits: Abstract and project page only. Survey experiments on attitudes, not nudges in field behaviour. Counts differ between versions. Correlation is across effects (ranking), not magnitude.
agent_relevance: An LLM can rank treatments better than chance but will overstate gains. To choose scaffold variants, use it only to rank candidates and always shrink.

source: DellaVigna and Pope (2018) Predicting Experimental Results: Who Knows What? (JPE; NBER w22566)
finding: Gap 3. Human forecasters: the average of many beats nearly all individuals, but experts do not beat non-experts at rank-ordering treatments.
numbers: 208 academic experts forecast 15 treatments in a real-effort task; also PhD students, undergraduates, MBAs, an online sample. Average forecast beat 96% of individual forecasts. Citations, rank and field did not improve accuracy.
limits: Abstract page only. Lab-style real-effort task, not a nudge megastudy. No correlation figure in the abstract.
agent_relevance: Individual forecasts of which variant wins are weak; pool many raters or measure. Supports G7: measure before keeping.

source: Choi, Laibson, Madrian, Metrick (2001) For Better or For Worse: Default Effects and 401(k) Savings Behavior (NBER w8651)
finding: Gap 10. Default side effect confirmed in three firms: participation rose above 85% but many stuck at a low default rate and a conservative fund, so wealth gains partly offset.
numbers: Three large firms. Participation above 85%. Default rate 2% or 3% and conservative fund. About 80% accepted both at first; after three years half still at default rate and fund only. Wealth effects roughly offset on average. Savings of the lowest savers rose.
limits: Abstract page only. Administrative data, non-randomised (firm policy change).
agent_relevance: Defaults help on the chosen dimension; unchosen dimensions anchor. For scaffold defaults (format, effort cap) log side effects on answer length, style and untouched quality dimensions. Human analogy only.

finding: Gaps 6 and 9 could not be researched: the WebSearch budget was exhausted and the Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex and arXiv API endpoints returned rate-limit errors. A PMC page returned a captcha.
numbers: Failed calls: Semantic Scholar 429 (several), OpenAlex insufficient budget, arXiv export 429, PMC reCAPTCHA. No preregistered large nudge trial and no new debiasing-at-equal-tokens study were found.
limits: This is a search-failure record, not a finding. Gaps 6 and 9 are unsearched, not negative.
agent_relevance: Retry gap 6 (debiasing at equal tokens; decoy, framing, omission) and gap 9 (preregistered structure-nudge trials) when search budget returns.
